tasks.short: Plan and develop new products and production processes

steps.what: Clarify new product requirements and identify production process constraints with specialists
Develop and trial candidate production methods with operators and technical specialists
Evaluate trials and plan proposed product and process development changes

tasks.design: Use existing {DOCS} requirements and {PROJECT} development records to support the supervisor's contribution to product and process development. Retain requirement clarification, shop-floor trials and evaluation; a production scheduling capability does not establish an ability to invent or validate a new process.
tasks.previous_blocker: New methods have uncertain physical behaviour and must fit real equipment and operator practice.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can organise trials, but this digest supplies no evidence that they remove the supervisor's development judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing useful trials, interpreting failures and balancing quality, safety, cost and throughput.
tasks.human_edge: Notice an unmodelled practical constraint and change the development direction with technical colleagues.
tasks.altitude: No change in development responsibility or authority to release a product or process.

reach.task: Contribute to a controlled production-method trial
reach.learn: Trial design, process limits and evidence needed for engineering approval

evidence.claim: Production development needs empirical trials and contextual interpretation; scheduling existing orders does not validate a new process.

assumptions: Boundary covers the supervisor's production contribution to development, not the product designer's work, engineering certification or commercial release. Other participants' time remains outside and unchanged.

Product specialists produce requirements through existing design work; the supervisor clarifies acceptance needs and constraints in s1. The supervisor produces trial observations and limitations in s2, with all capture time counted; no free structured trial-result feed is assumed.

Unclear requirements and missing measurements return to direct clarification or another controlled trial, not generated conclusions. Existing safety and engineering permissions for trials remain mandatory and unchanged; this design automates no physical action.
Test native trial-record and project functions before future custom tools; none is proposed here.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new software, measurements or reporting process is introduced. Process planning overlap with other tasks is allocated once.
unknowns: Supervisor development remit, trial permissions and current recording burden
research_questions: Which measured clerical step, if any, consumes time after trial interpretation is complete?

already_counted.description: Requirement work, trial contribution, interpretation and planning remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=net=0. Incremental product changes and uncertain new processes retain all development work; no hypothetical design or trial automation saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The supervisor retains the same role in translating product needs into practical production development.
reach: Contribute to controlled process trials with machinists
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who records clear limitations and helps technical colleagues choose the next useful trial; this task design releases no measured time.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Production and Operating Workers
